title: Article: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
summary:
Moving GenAI into high-stakes production requires treating non-determinism as an engineering problem. This architectural blueprint shows engineering leaders and architects how to build trustworthy agentic workflows using knowledge graphs, dual-layer eval judges, CI/CD release gates, and regression testing against golden datasets to automate drafting while maintaining zero-hallucination compliance.

By Ritesh Modi, Sasidhar Gudala

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI
summary:
At QCon San Francisco 2026, OpenAI's Brian Yang described building the ChatGPT ads product with Codex agents and no human-written code. He outlined layered testing, sandboxes, and batched pull request reviews, and noted failure modes such as code "slop" and unsafe agent actions. He advised gradual adoption and framed engineers as managers of agents.

By Daniel Curtis

title: JEP 545 Moves ZGC Memory Preparation off the Startup Path in JDK 28
summary:
JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, has been integrated into JDK 28, moving heap memory preparation onto concurrent worker threads. ZGC now pre-touches memory as it expands and upgrades small pages to large ones on Linux 6.1 and later, but the 2 MB initial heap behind the JEP's 38% startup and 90% warmup gains requires the adaptive heap sizing flag from JEP 546, which is off by default.

By A N M Bazlur Rahman

title: Agoda Reduces API Code Review Time by 64% with Modular Architecture
summary:
Agoda introduced a modular monolith framework in its post-booking API to reduce coupling without a full rewrite. The platform uses domain components, Data Mapper patterns, typed builders, and ArchUnit tests to enforce boundaries. Framework-backed changes showed 64% shorter median code reviews and 34% faster initial feedback than legacy changes.

By Leela Kumili

title: Podcast: Simulation Can Tell You What Your Agents are Actually Doing: A Conversation with Zhou Yu
summary:
Michael Stiefel spoke to Zhou Yu about using dynamic simulations to evaluate AI agents. One particular focus was conversational agents where actions depend on prior responses, and the non-deterministic nation of LLMs means you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks. You need to test them using dynamic simulations that incorporate different personas, goals, and corner cases.

By Zhou Yu

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Harness Is the New Operating System
summary:
At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mad Labs founder and CEO Manju Rajashekhar opened the conference arguing that the harness around an AI model, rather than the model itself, decides what an agent can do and how safely it does it. The keynote mapped the parts of a harness, including context, tools, state, permissions and feedback loops, onto jobs that operating systems already perform.

By Andrew Hoblitzell

title: Claude Code Has Been Leaking Secrets through its "Don't Ask Again" Feature
summary:
Agentic security firm Apiiro found that Claude Code has been exposing secrets in public repositories due to how it stores them in local file on developers' machines to implement "Don't Ask Again". The company identified 1,122 secrets in claude/settings.local.json files and another 1,160 in git history, in the shared settings.json, and in agent chat transcripts stored in repos.

By Sergio De Simone

title: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
summary:
Google recently announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service that runs AI agents in isolated microVMs, with checkpointing capabilities to suspend and resume execution environments. The design keeps credentials, API keys, and OAuth refresh tokens outside the agent sandbox, using an external Agent Gateway to authenticate requests and inject the required secrets.

By Renato Losio

title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
summary:
AWS Lambda now runs Event Functions on EC2 G-series GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU, vLLM and SGLang base images that need no handler code, and 90-minute asynchronous timeouts. Billing is the instance price plus a 9.75 percent fee; first hands-on tests report an eight-minute publish and no response streaming.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers
